messages:
alex_ng: paging oncall — p99 spike hitting several customers in eu-west-1, seeing streaming stalls during token stream; customers reporting stalled completions :phone:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: routing-latency-spike detected. Severity: P1. Trigger: router tail latency > 10s at p99 for 3m. Pager: jamie_oncall@pagerduty
jamie_oncall: I’m on it, switching to phone. Can someone paste the p95/p99 numbers and affected routes?
maria_g: p95 ~ 450ms -> baseline. p99 jumped from ~1.2s to 12s over last 6m. Top routes: /v1/generate (chat-streaming), /v1/stream. Region: mostly eu-west-1, a couple hits in us-west-2.
cheng_li: Seeing a pattern in router logs — a subset of shards are getting hot connection counts. Hash distribution skewed. Possible hot-partition on routing-table bucket 42.
ryan_platform: Confirmed. Router LB mapping shows weight drift — a policy rollout that modified routing weights an hour ago (canary): policy id: pol-2024-09-11-1732
alex_ng: oh — that policy was supposed to be read-only for canary. Did the rollout accidentally flip to global? @ryan_platform can you check rollout state?
ryan_platform: digging. It looks like the rollout job retried and applied to all zones due to an idempotency bug. A rollback was attempted but some routers didn't pick up the config due to TTL caching.
maria_g: Impacted routers are forwarding to a tiny set of active backends -> hot queues -> streaming stalls. Correlates with KV cache pressure on those backends.
jamie_oncall: Customer-impact estimate? Which customers are affected?
ash_cs: I've got two customers in my queue: AcmeAnalytics (eu-west-1) and BetaChat (global). Acme is showing 30% of requests timing out in last 10m. BetaChat reports intermittent stalls in chat UIs.
cheng_li: Proposed mitigation: reduce routing weight for the misrouted bucket, enable eager-fallback to secondary model variant for streaming, and increase KV cache TTL to reduce backend load. Patch commands below.
cheng_li: ```
# temporary mitigation: set weight 0.1 for bucket 42
redwoodctl routing update --policy pol-2024-09-11-1732 --bucket 42 --weight 0.1
# enable eager fallback
redwoodctl config set global.eager_fallback true --ttl 1800
``` 
jamie_oncall: Go for it. Prioritize weight adjustment first.
ryan_platform: Applying weight change now. Pushing to routers with low TTL first.
incident-bot: ACTION TAKEN: routing weight update submitted by ryan_platform. Job id: job-7721. Rolling out to zone eu-west-1.
maria_g: After partial rollout, p99 dropped from 12s -> ~3.1s in eu-west-1 but still above SLO. Streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated.
alex_ng: Thanks. Next step: drain the most overloaded backend instances behind bucket 42 and re-balance. Can we autoscale those pools?
ryan_platform: Autoscale blocked because those instances are hitting a memory KV cache oom threshold. Need a graceful drain: mark nodes read-only then spawn replacements.
cheng_li: I'll run the drain. Command:
cheng_li: ```
redwoodctl nodes drain --pool bk-42 --timeout 600
redwoodctl nodes add --pool bk-42 --count 3 --instance-type rtx-48
``` 
jamie_oncall: Execute the drain when weight update is fully propagated. Want to avoid cascading failures.
ryan_platform: Weight rollout finished across eu-west-1. Proceed with drain in 2m.
ash_cs: Customers are getting status updates. AcmeAnalytics replied: "We're seeing improvement but occasional stalls persist." They asked for ETA.
jamie_oncall: Tell them we're mitigating now, expect observable improvement within 10-20 minutes, full stabilization 30-45m.
alex_ng: Also open: why did policy retried and apply globally? Need postmortem item. @ryan_platform please capture the rollout job logs (job-4382 and job-4382-retry).
ryan_platform: already grabbing logs. Root cause looks like the retry path in rollout orchestration didn't respect the canary flag when encountering 409. Will create a fix branch.
incident-bot: METRICS SNAPSHOT: eu-west-1 /v1/stream: p95=760ms p99=3.1s error-rate=4.6% before drains. After weight+drain: p95=310ms p99=1.4s error-rate=1.1%
maria_g: Good trend. Some residuals from us-west-2—those routers had older config TTLs. We should push a targeted purge to force config reload.
cheng_li: Doing a config-purge for old routers in us-west-2.
cheng_li: ```
redwoodctl routing purge-cache --zone us-west-2 --policy pol-2024-09-11-1732
``` 
ryan_platform: Purge done. us-west-2 p99 back to baseline ~1.2s. eu-west-1 nearly stabilized.
jamie_oncall: Any customer-facing escalations? @ash_cs
ash_cs: AcmeAnalytics opened a support ticket expressing high severity. We've sent interim update and offered to apply tenant-specific fallback. No legal/regulatory exposures.
alex_ng: Next steps: (1) keep monitoring for 1h, (2) rollback the faulty rollout job to restore original canary semantics, (3) patch rollout orchestration to honor canary on retries, (4) postmortem and action items.
jamie_oncall: I’ll own the rollback & postmortem. Assigning action to ryan_platform for orchestration fix, cheng_li for draining playbook updates, maria_g for metrics dashboards and alert tuning.
ryan_platform: Acknowledged. Creating rollback now.
incident-bot: ACTION TAKEN: rollback job job-4382-rollback started by jamie_oncall. Expected duration 3m.
jamie_oncall: Rolling to resolved when p99 stabilizes below 1.5s and error-rate <1.5% for 15 consecutive minutes.
maria_g: We're at p99=1.2s and error-rate=0.9% for the last 7m. Continue to monitor.
ash_cs: Acme confirmed improvement: "Thanks—latency is back to acceptable levels. We’ll keep an eye out." :white_check_mark:
jamie_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated. Will kick off postmortem doc and timeline in #incidents-postmortems. Preliminary severity P1->P2 after mitigation.
alex_ng: Thanks everyone. Longer-term: add unit test for rollout retry semantics + alert to detect config drift between control plane and routers.
ryan_platform: Will include fix and a canary-only enforcement in next deployment.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status= mitigated. Duration: ~38m. Pager released for jamie_oncall.
jamie_oncall: Signing off. If anything pops, reopen thread. :lock:
